curriculum.lesson_evidence: A citizen is a member of a community with rights and responsibilities. Good citizens follow laws and rules, respect other people, care for shared places, help others and take part in decisions in ways that suit their age, such as class votes.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.child_mission: A citizen is a member of a community with rights and responsibilities. Good citizens follow laws and rules, respect other people, care for shared places, help others and take part in decisions in ways that suit their age, such as class votes.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which are good citizen actions: picking up litter in a park; copying in a test; volunteering at the school fete; leaving a gate open on a farm?

FEEDBACK
Picking up litter and volunteering. Copying is dishonest and an open farm gate can harm animals and people.

WATCH FOR
Believing only adults can be citizens ignores the many ways children contribute to their communities.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write a citizenship plan with three actions, one for home, one for school and one for the wider community. For each name the responsibility it shows and how you will record evidence that you did it.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
